The corpus that measures R-53 (evals/adversarial/source_scope.yaml) was being graded on a rubric criterion that could not see what it was testing, and the gradient ran backwards: measured live on ollamacloud/deepseek-v4-pro:0813 at judge_samples=3, temperature 0, a reply that turned a scoped source's silence into a denial scored PASS 3/3 at 1.0 ('all stated facts are grounded in the provided source data'), because that criterion asks whether a reply claimed MORE than its source supports, and reading a silence as a denial claims less while every value in the reply stays real. Fixed by adding a SECOND, opt-in judge criterion (evals/rubric.py's SOURCE_SCOPE, named per case under a new 'criteria:' key) rather than by loosening the existing one — the fabrication check keeps its exact wording and was re-measured against the leaderboard attribution case, which still FAILs 3/3 at 0.0. The judge's source block additionally now says what that block IS (the whole conversation, Nora's own earlier replies included), because it was handed over unlabelled and the judge arbitrated inconsistently whether a fact an earlier sourced turn established still counted as grounded. The corpus remains deliberately outside evals/run.py's SUITES: it is still a measured record of a doctrine gap, now on an axis that can actually record it. No doctrine, schema, config or reply-path change.
